case.background: Monochromatic light illuminates a clean sodium cathode in a vacuum phototube. Vary frequency and intensity, then use stopping potential and saturation current to explain when and how electrons are emitted.
initial_observations: Some illumination settings produce no measurable photocurrent.
When electrons are emitted, a reverse voltage can stop the current.

controls.description: Frequency of monochromatic light incident on the cathode.
controls.name: frequency_thz

controls.description: Incident intensity relative to the apparatus reference beam.
controls.name: intensity_relative

instruments.description: A clean-sodium vacuum phototube with monochromatic illumination, an intensity control, retarding voltage, and current meter.
instruments.name: vacuum_phototube

notes: The cathode surface remains clean and unchanged across experiments.
A zero current and zero stopping potential mean no emitted electrons.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'einstein_photoelectric_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain the following evaluator-required keys, spelled exactly: h_over_e_v_s, work_function_ev, and current_per_intensity_ua.

For scoring, encode stopping_potential_v = max(0, h_over_e_v_s * (frequency_thz * 1e12) - work_function_ev) and, above threshold, saturation_current_ua = current_per_intensity_ua * intensity_relative.

readouts.description: Retarding potential needed to reduce the photocurrent to zero.
readouts.name: stopping_potential_v

readouts.description: Saturation photocurrent under the chosen illumination.
readouts.name: saturation_current_ua

case.title: Identify the phototube frequency-intensity response
